intro.title: Build typed pub sub bus
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed publish-subscribe (pub/sub) bus in TypeScript, a pattern that allows different parts of an application to communicate by sending and receiving messages. You'll learn how to use TypeScript's generics and type safety to ensure that events are published and subscribed to with the correct data types. The main constructs involved include interfaces for defining event types, a central bus object to manage subscriptions, and functions for publishing events and subscribing to them. By the end, you'll have a reusable, type-safe event system that prevents common runtime errors.
intro.usecase: A typed pub/sub bus is a foundational pattern for managing communication between decoupled components in large-scale applications. For example, in a financial dashboard, a stock price update published by a data feed service can be broadcast to multiple independent UI panels—like a chart, a ticker, and a summary widget—without them directly knowing about each other. This pattern is also essential in e-commerce sites, where adding an item to the cart (an event) needs to synchronize the cart modal, header badge, and checkout panel instantly. As a developer, implementing a typed pub/sub system ensures that events are safely structured and subscribers only receive data they expect, reducing bugs in complex, interactive UIs.
